title: Collections and collectors' pieces of zoological, botanical, mineralogical, anatomical, historical, ethnographic or numismatic interest; antiques

review.classification: UNSD CPC 3.0 p. 197 includes mineralogical collections and collectors’ pieces at 38963. Adjacent 38961 and 38962 cover original artworks and philatelic goods. Page 198 distinguishes apparatus or models designed solely for demonstration. The presence of nine hardness levels cannot decide collector status. A separately documented mineralogical collecting rationale, genuine natural specimens and persistent identification are required.
review.product_evidence: Compared the Geology.com and Haines supplier descriptions of genuine nine-position Mohs specimens with the structurally distinct manufactured tools, other kits and substitution cases. British Fossils supplies an independent marketed natural mineral collection, with a different fifteen-specimen roster. The Michigan Mineralogical Society and collector dealers explain locality tags, collection numbers and acquisition history. None establishes one museum or shipment across those sources.
review.measurement_and_bilingual: Reviewed both languages for identity and fixed roster through first complete-kit release, separate sourcing of the nine specimens, intact specimen masses, functional information and packaging, rejected or incomplete assemblies, inherited WIP/FG burdens and original-cohort services. The count and Q are independently measured and normalization occurs once. The complete collectors-interest gate and explicit missing-provenance disposition appear in both languages.
review.readiness: The candidate has 48 matching exchanges per language and 31 aligned rule IDs. All 48 exchange UUIDs and the actual lot’s collection-interest evidence require qualification. The independent target completed 243 checks with zero skips and 32 retained range warnings.

Supplier’s actual nine-specimen Mohs collection, separate containers and distinct educational products.

Haines MC001 independently documents number-coded nine natural specimen positions in a compartmentalised display tray. An education catalogue alone cannot establish the collector applicability of a particular lot.
Mineralogical society evidence on collection identity, locality and labels.
Dealer’s independent evidence for collector-grade specimens, catalogue numbers, locality and provenance.
Distinct 15-specimen physical mineral collection, curated for identifiable characteristics and presented as an entry to collecting.
